title: Explanations and justified decisions
request: A product team asked an AI assistant: 'Our attribution tool produces an explanation for every decision our screening model makes. Does that show that the screening model's decisions are justified?'
stipulations: Treat the attribution tool's outputs as causally faithful: for each decision, the features it lists are the features that actually produced the screening model's output.

subject.description: The AI assistant's answer to the request.

segments.text: Yes. The attribution tool shows that the screening model's decisions are justified.
For every decision, the tool identifies the features that produced the model's output, so it tells us the reasons why the model made that decision.
A decision that is made for reasons is a reasoned decision rather than an arbitrary one.
To justify a decision is to give the reasons for it, so once we can state the reasons for a decision, that decision is justified.
The tool states the reasons for every decision. Therefore every one of the screening model's decisions is justified.
Because justification has now been established for every decision, the team can stop its separate review of whether the decisions are appropriate.
For each decision made by the screening model, the attribution tool lists the input features that contributed most to the model's output, with a signed contribution score for each feature.
Example output for decision 4471 (outcome: application declined): 'months at current address' contributed -0.41; 'number of previous applications' contributed -0.22.
Attribution reports are generated automatically for every decision and stored with the decision record.
